title: Square-zero algebra extensions with a specified kernel and their diagrams
statement: For a homomorphism $R\to A$ of commutative rings and an $A$-module $M$, a square-zero algebra extension consists of a commutative ring $E$, maps $R\to E\xrightarrow{p}A$ with their composite the given base map, and an additive injection $i:M\to E$ such that $p$ is surjective, $\ker(p)=i(M)$, $i(m)i(n)=0$, and $e i(m)=i(p(e)m)$. An extension map over $f:A\to B$ and an additive kernel map $u:M\to N$ is a ring map commuting with the base, quotient and kernel maps; when used in coefficient changes, $u$ is linear for the restricted action. An extension isomorphism is a ring isomorphism fixing the base, quotient and specified kernel. A split extension is identified additively with the existing trivial square-zero extension $A\oplus M$ [def-sc-trivial-square-zero-extension], preserving the base and kernel inclusions, quotient projection, and multiplication $(a,m)(b,n)=(ab,an+bm)$. A coefficient pushout along $u:M\to N$ has a map inducing $u$, universal among such maps into extensions with kernel $N$. A fibre product of two extensions over $A$ has kernel $M\oplus M$ with the two kernel projections, and its maps biject its elements with pairs of elements having equal quotient. A Baer sum is this fibre product followed by coefficient pushout along addition $M\oplus M\to M$. These are data and predicates; no existence is asserted.
